pages.title: Bertha
text: Bertha is a lady of contradictions. She could be described equally as a doctor with an appreciation for the importance of killing, or a killer with a strong interest in helping the sick and needy. For the sick, infirm, and injured, Bertha is a brave and confident medical professional who spares no effort in speeding up the recovery of those under her care. For those that Bertha deems insufficiently appreciative of others, or worse, plagues upon humanity, she takes on the role of eraser of evil from the human experience. In keeping with the medical theme of Bertha's work, she has even chosen a strange type of weapon modeled after an enormous syringe, which symbolizes her philosophy that "the best medicine is sometimes the one that kills the patient." Bertha's evolution to punisher of the wayward began with an idyllic childhood in a wealthy city-state. Known as a hub of the most advanced medicine anywhere on the Tundra, Bertha was proud to walk in the footsteps of those around her. She too swore an oath to do no harm when helping others. After all, she thought, "Isn't the Tundra cold enough as it is? Only the hopeful spark of humanity out there in the bitter cold can give purpose to our lives." Years of training gave Bertha the skills to be considered one of the top nurses in her city. A chance encounter here provided Bertha with another view of the potential side-effects of the nurse's creed and the consequences of neutrality. A high-ranking general presented Bertha's to ward with severe injuries. Bertha and many high-profile doctors did their best to nurse the lady-commander back to health. The sense of achievement was short-lived. Shortly after the general was discharged, a steady stream of bandit attacks began to hit neighboring cities. These attacks only increased in viciousness until finally even Bertha's city saw a touch of the desolation and fire spreading elsewhere. Only when a significant bounty was posted for the bandit leader's arrest did Bertha finally realize their enemy was in fact the so-called "general" whose life they had saved that day in the operating theater: Queen of Violence, Zenobia. "Do no harm" had made Bertha and her team accomplices to the deaths of thousands. As Zenobia continued her reign of terror, Bertha was forced to confront the cost of wielding only a scalpel of healing rather than of death. Her soul-searching ended when she realized that just as she might cut a disease out of a sick patient, she must also help humanity by cleansing evil from the Tundra. Bertha had found new purpose in life: cleansing the world of the more subtle disease of lawbreakers, bandits, and all others who practice the poison of selfishness. Queen Zenobia would fall one day, but in the meantime all evildoers would be fair game for her needle of justice. As she herself says: "Death is also a cure for disease."

pages.title: Seigel
text: Seigel is the strongest of the Night's Guard by far. The roaming "Shield of Hell" is also far more tenacious than any other member of the Guard, able to endure battle for days in Hell's dark mist. Seigel is a shield both literally and physically. He stands between fellow soldiers and the horrors beyond. Seigel can do all these things because he is the man who returned from the land of crystal death. No signs of insanity or the rage of the Blood Moon show themselves in him even if his body is slightly deformed. If Seigel still suffers anything from his time behind the veil of Hell it is only the loss of his memories. If memories "make the man", then Seigel is both lucky and cursed. Whatever pain there was has been left behind. For he is a blank sheet now, free to engage in what gives him meaning: fighting alongside his brothers-in-arms! Viveca stumbled across Seigel on a patrol into the heartland of Hell, still infested by Blood Moon Plague sufferers. Overconfident in their arms, Viveca allowed her men to be cornered by a sudden ambush. Empty city streets were suddenly filled by violent, twisted beings. It is hard to say if Viveca would have survived without help. Seigel suddenly burst through the encirclement, cutting a path with a viciousness Viveca used to escape. "It was like watching a golem lay in to a whirlwind of red claws as Seigel threw twisted limbs onto the scrapheap!" Seigel's exploits became more than a rescue by a mortal man in their retelling. Once Viveca and her men reached a safe distance they turned to help Seigel, who was covered with scars that should have laid him six feet under. Not only did Seigel recover quickly but showed no signs himself of being infected. When a shocked Viveca asked how he had traveled so far into infected territory, he said he had been living there for months... perhaps years. Seigel was given a guard of honor back to the Night's Guard headquarters where Philly conducted a thorough physical examination—from a safe distance. She found Seigel had miraculously escaped unscathed from Blood Moon infection. Or at least that was the report Philly revealed to the Night's Guard... The Guard were happy to induct a survivor of inhuman strength into their ranks and crowned him with an honorific previously given to one of their fallen comrades. Seigel's great fighting strength was then enhanced by a long spear and coat of spike armor with which he could stand at the vanguard. The reservations of Seigel's brothers-in-arms were quickly dispelled by his protective valor. With each fellow Guardsman's life saved, Seigel built trust among the troops. He would surely be a captain now were it not for his apparent lack of humor and inability to understand the finer cues of human interaction. Philly and Viveca have not been entirely forthcoming about Seigel's true nature. Philly's examination did not reveal Seigel escaped the Blood Moon Plague, but the opposite: he showed every sign of infection in his blood serum. In fact, Seigel was much closer to an infected than an ordinary human being at a microscopic level. Yet somehow he had managed to retain his own humanity, now boosted by inhuman strength. Philly has conjectured that in many ways Seigel could be described as another life form, not fully human, nor infected. Only time will tell if it can be called "superior". Far more interesting to Viveca are his recollections of Hell. "I always knew there was a presence out there in the mist... calling to me. Trying to establish contact," Seigel remarked in interviews kept confidential from others. "It was a person and not a person—perhaps many people. It was trying to show me how it saw the world. I knew if I let myself see the world through its eyes, it would be more wonderful and stranger than I could imagine..." Seigel described feeling hate for the Entity by instinct. His heart rose up to bite its welcoming hand. Then the Entity's voice grew more distant, especially after joining the Night's Guard. Only time can tell whether Viveca can use Seigel's experiences to gain a better understanding of their enemy.

pages.title: Aisha
text: "I have come to bring judgment upon the treacherous and unfaithful!" It was not until Aisha saw the brilliant white snow of the sunlit Tundra, squinting against the brightness of the light, that she knew in her heart the depth of what she had lost. Time, so much time. Even the empire founded by her betrayers had itself almost been wholly eaten up by time. But if there were still some chance to punish her betrayers, she would take it. First, vengeance would have to wait until more practical tasks had been accomplished: the rebinding of Aisha's lineage into a single clan under her rule. Her new kingdom would have to be at least as powerful as her old one, but more united. Unity was a prerequisite for vengeance. Aisha's era passed out of living memory long ago. But in the world of old she had been a queen of royal blood, and not only a queen but a priestess too. She had been taught well in the ways of the living Fire Crystals, their communion, power, and divination. In those days, the people considered their priests and nobles to be gods. Aisha was noble enough to realize that the gods had nothing to do with it. Their power really came from their mastery over Fire Crystals, plain and simple. And also the machines that interfaced with the Fire Crystals, the Obelisks of Light or the artifices of the royal palaces—all brilliant creations of tribes even more ancient about whom little was known, but much was inherited. The same relics that gave Aisha's clan power to rule also shrouded her dynasty in self-doubt and secrecy. The fact that Aisha's power ultimately came from others' technology made it much easier for ambitious Chiefs to rebel. Civil strife reached a high point during Aisha's reign as the outlying tribes—one was even then named Phaethon—attacked the palace to take the keys of Aisha's kingdom for themselves. By the time of Aisha's reign, her dynasty had already well and truly lost its aura of divinity. Her kingdom powerful still, but not for a war against all. It was in this era that a foreign-born legion of cavalry mercenaries offered their assistance. Joining their forces to Aisha's protected the palace for a number of seasons. The foreign mercenaries had won Aisha's trust. Better yet, they seemed wholly reliant upon her authority unlike her own people, and thus better placed to share in the secrets of its defense. Aisha revealed many mysteries to the foreigners, including those of Cthugha's Heart and how to wield the ancient devices used to protect the palace. It was in this moment of triumph, when Aisha seemed to have defeated the rebels, that the foreigners struck. Aisha's bodyguards were suddenly slaughtered. She herself only just escaped with her life. In the end, despite winning the war, Aisha ended up losing the keys to her kingdom anyway. And what made it so much harder to accept was that it was because of treachery. Worse yet, the traitors went on to found their own disgusting dynasty, the so-called "Solaris Empire" in the ruins of what her ancestors had accomplished! Aisha fled along secret pathways only she could know, the traitors hot on her heels. There was one way and only one way to save her life. Yet in some respects, it was not much better than death. Indeed, it would mimic death. Aisha cautiously inserted herself into the tiny coffin-sarcophagus—another gift of the ancestors although in their time they had called it a "capsule", and felt her heartbeat slowing. This was the cryogenic death that she had read about but never witnessed. She would have nothing more to do with the world until she was awoken from her sleep-death. But hopefully that day would come soon. The day of Aisha's awakening did not come as soon as she had hoped. Not many knew of Aisha's plan, and those that did were either killed or fled with no chance to come to her aid. Buried away beneath a labyrinth of mazes, only the most determined tomb raider could ever come to her side. And so it was that Aisha's name almost passed out of living memory until she was awoken by just such a grave robber. As the capsule hissed and steam began pouring into the chamber, the wide-eyed grave robber did not stick around to hear an explanation. Nor was Aisha about to demand an explanation from the man fleeing down the corridor. Her thoughts were only filled with anger and grief at what she had lost: the power rightfully hers, the authority she must one day regain. She must regain it if she is ever to correct the scales of history.

pages.title: Nikola
text: "Looks like I've shocked you! Bwahaha!" The crazy man standing in front of the electrocuted foe, laughing manically, teeth bared in a kind of disturbing grin, is none other than Nikola the lightning warrior. It's not clear exactly how rumors of Nikola's shocking powers began, but it is clear that he has since become a kind of boogeyman, a magical mercenary of the Tundra feared far and wide for his lightning bolts. Of course, Nikola is not really a walking spirit, angel, demon, or extraterrestrial, but just an ordinary man. What is not ordinary about him is his "Arc Generator" wherein in his true power lies. His most remarkable superpower, if there be any, is his incredible skill as an inventor. Before Nikola was the lightning warrior he was about as far from a roving mercenary as you could imagine—he was an inventor, and how he got to where he is today constitutes a tale. Nikola was known more for his shyness, hesitation, and even self-doubt in his previous life as an inventor—certainly not for maniacally electrocuting enemies, of which at the time there were none. Nikola had always been a rather unusual child. Ever since his parents encouraged his interest in science in his remote home city, he devoted himself heart and soul to a scientific understanding of the cosmos. He quickly became obsessed with electricity as a means of lighting and heating rather than the more popular steam-based methods, which he thought primitive. Nikola soon found himself with wealthy sponsors willing to bankroll his efforts in the promising new science of electricity. Nikola couldn't have been happier—until, that is, Fire Crystals emerged. Nikola realized to his annoyance that Fire Crystals were a better, more readily available source of energy and heat than what his "electricity" could deliver (even if explosive). And the kinds of Chiefs who had been willing to throw money Nikola's way were also the kinds of Chiefs most excited about Fire Crystals. Nikola soon found his research funds and sponsors had disappeared. Of course, Nikola's raw talent could not be defeated by a mere total lack of money. He was determined, more than ever, to turn his dreams of electrical energy into reality. Unfortunately for Nikola, reality is often disappointing. No more money meant no more assistants. No more money meant worse equipment, if any. No more money meant Nikola was in a race against time whether he wanted it or not: either he would come up with a working solution soon, or his equipment would fail, or he would blow himself up, or some combination of the above. When Nikola finally produced a working product after so many sleepless marathons, he discovered it was actually inferior to existing Fire Crystal products already on the market. He was also in enormous debt. This was his darkest hour, and in his darkest hour one of his friends suggested a solution so obvious Nikola could hardly believe he hadn't thought of it himself: "You know what Chiefs love? Weapons! So what if it's a bad heater? Can you at least shoot it?" Of course! Even if being known as an arms dealer was maybe not quite as good as being known as an inventor, selling weapons could open a lot of doors... doors perhaps to make other dreams come true. Many more months of hard work later and Nikola finally had his masterpiece: the "Arc Generator". A working prototype needs to work, and there's no better way to experiment with weapons than on a real battlefield—even if Nikola was the lab rat. Nikola exchanged a lab coat for a mercenary's uniform and began offering the chance to partake in the future of weaponry to anybody who would listen for a low price or even no price at all. Instead of real funds, it was time to collect real data. The legend of Nikola the lightning warrior was born in the "laboratory of the battlefield" as he put it. A few releases of Nikola's pent-up rage, anger and frustration at having his genius unrecognized was all it took. In the smoking remains of Nikola's enemies came a lot of orders for the new Arc Generator. Finally having some real money has not put a dent in Nikola's ambitions, which have only grown larger and more unhinged since his newfound success. Now he wishes to upscale his invention to a more magnificent tower full of electrical coils. If his calculations are correct, it will unleash such a terrifying lightning storm across the Tundra as has never been seen. Nikola is a man on a mission to build it. And if he does, war on the Tundra might not look the same again.

pages.title: Jordan
text: Home is by the sunset beaches of Skylark, a trading city known far and wide as a meeting place of all good wares, cultures, stories, music, stories and legends across the Tundra. Skylark's riches have also brought their fair share of trouble, particularly from bandits and invaders eager for their share. Invaders from sea will have to pass through one main obstacle before helping themselves, but it is a powerful obstacle: Jordan and his "Cornflower Dreadnought", a steel wall that breaks waves and invaders in equal measure. The eldest son of the City Chief, preparations had been made from Jordan's birth for him to inherit the leadership. But it became evident from an early age that sitting still upon a throne was not for young Jordan. His dreams were always turning to the blue foam and white sails of the distant ocean. So it was that he bid farewell to his father's city as soon as he was able to spend ten years at sea. It would be an understatement to say the seafaring life was a learning experience for Jordan. It certainly did broaden his horizons. He returned home to find his younger brother had, as he had expected, inherited the throne. He received a hero's welcome and the offer of a new responsibility: safeguarding the city's coast at the head of his own fleet. Jordan took to his coastguard admiralty with so much enthusiasm, the city's accountants began to fear Jordan was wasting its riches on unproven steam propulsion upgrades to the aging fleet. But whatever worries the bean counters may have had about the cost-effectiveness of steam engines were soon put to rest. Just after the retrofit had been completed, the city went on to experience the mother of all sea battles. While Skylark had been enjoying peace and prosperity, neighboring states envious of its success had begun working hand-in-glove with Crazy Joe's bandits to take it. Regular naval forces and sea bandits led an all-out assault on Skylark without warning. Worse yet, many of the mercenaries the city had paid to protect it were lured by Crazy Joe and the promise of easy coin to flee the city in its hour of need. Jordan's ships were the only thing standing between a fleet more than twice its size and doom. But few knew the ins and outs of naval warfare like Jordan, nor what his new steam ships were capable of. As night fell and the wind died, Jordan crashed headlong into the main enemy fleet. Utter chaos ensued with shots, screams and cannonfire raging. Jordan even took a few rounds himself, but it did nothing to weaken his overwhelming sense of victory. By the time sunlight filtered its way past the distant horizon, Crazy Joe's forces had fled. The few regular ships still afloat were waving the white flag. Jordan's heroism went down in history that day and earned the eternal admiration of Skylark's people. He could have used his newfound stature to commission a fleet of similar dreadnoughts. But after showing his city what must be done, he unexpectedly resigned his admiralty to undertake what to cityfolk must have seemed an utterly baffling journey. Much of Jordan's life had been lived in the shadow of an event that happened when he nearly drowned as a young boy. While others would have been terrified of water from that point on, Jordan experienced a kind of vision in the water—a vision of a grand underwater metropolis full of love, warmth and peace. And it was this vision—rather than the terrifying experience of nearly losing his life—that he would come to associate with the water for the rest of his life. Everything changed when a sailor said Jordan's vision reminded him of a real place called the "Sunken Kingdom" one day in a salty sea inn when Jordan decided to open up about it. Jordan listened, awestruck as Hendrik shared what other sailors had seen or heard of the lost city. Jordan became more and more convinced that this vision was something more than a flight of fancy by an impressionable youth. It was a calling—a purpose. If the city given to him in a vision from his youth existed, then surely Jordan owed it to himself to follow this path to its truth, wherever it may lead, even if it meant embarking on a journey of dreams.

pages.title: Freya
text: Freya once thought the Tundra was the worst thing that could happen to the world. The Blood Moon Plague proved her wrong. The name of Freya's hometown has been lost to the history books. It is now known as Hell, the Land of No Return, or the Abandoned City. Its once vibrant streets are covered in fog. None approach. But if a lost traveler were to venture near, they might still hear something: screams and shouts to chill them to their bones. As a Nightguard, Freya and her fellow sentries were well-protected at the city outskirts inside a tower with plenty of food when the Blood Moon came. Never would they have guessed that one day they would not be defending against invaders, but preventing former family and friends from ever getting out. But someone always slips through. Words cannot describe the terror on a traveling merchant who, after wandering off a mountain path, came face to face with the monsters of Hell. Crooked, misshapen human things covered in grotesque scarlet crystal flower petals, their jet black eyes full of darkness and suffering. The next thing the merchant knew, the monsters had fallen to the ground with a glint of cold steel and he was being dragged back to a sentry tower by a shadowy figure. This lady—his unfriendly savior—said nothing as she called for a doctor to give a full examination. A strange figure in a bird mask examined the merchant carefully for a disease referred in hushed tones as the "Blood Moon Plague". Fortunately, he was allowed to go free with a strict warning and ominous feeling that if he had shown any signs whatsoever of the plague—whatever that was—he would have been treated very differently. Philly, investigator of all strange diseases, originally named it the Blood Moon Plague upon hearing Freya's harrowing account. The first rule of plague is to prevent its spread, which Philly urged the sentries to do. He struggled to come to terms with the mysterious illness that seemed to spread via crystals and fog, turning men into beasts with great speed. Freya was the exception who, once she recognized in her body the signs of infection, merely collapsed. So she was kept under observation. Eventually, as if by some miracle, she began to observe her own recovery. Her body's natural defenses began to survive, even thrive. Now she is the only one who can walk through Hell with impunity. Great strength has also come through the inactivated remnants of the disease in her body. Freya has since become a key member of her fellow Night's Guard survivors: a lady immune, with super strength, tasked with keeping the gates of Hell firmly closed. Hades was once called Metiya, a tiny city on the edge of the wilderness. Life in the age of ice and cold was a tough adjustment. The City's Furnace was often short of materials. It was in these desperate times a strange visitor arrived with a promise of abundance if he could run a little "experiment". It was a success at first. People gained great strength and energy even without food. They could walk outside without feeling the cold. But grotesque deformities soon followed, rage, and a terrible madness. In the end, the vast majority of "subjects" lost all reason and began attacking their neighbors. A fog descended at roughly the same time over the whole town, either a cause or consequence of the plague—Freya cannot say. She was then infected. As her eyes turned cold and red and dim she looked upward. The full moon should have been silver-gray. It was completely covered in blood. That is all Freya remembers of her long recovery. Now there is only the hope that just as she has healed, Hell's residents can do some too.

pages.title: Wu Ming
text: No one knows his real name, but every town has hard of his legend- As a warrior who wanders the land, Wu Ming has made a name for himself as a martial artist. He reached a high level of perfection in his skills, and is not adraid to use his strength to help the weak. His chivalry has earned him an excellent reputation, and with his Dragonslayer in hand, he is a terror to the opportunistic bandits who roam the Tundra. Though he has become accustomed to the life of a wanderer, he still stays temporily in poorer towns to teach Survivor how to protec themselves. After all, like an old saying from his distant hometown, "Teach a man to fish, and you feed him for a lifetime." Wu Ming is skilled not just in martial arts, but in music and the arts. However, what people praise more about him is his humbleness and amiable personality. He would even play the role of a schoolteacher in the town sometimes and teach children how to read, write, and count. He also tells them fantastical myths from foreign lands. Few know that Wu Ming was once a person who was completely different than his current self. His past self's only pursuit in life was to go down in history as the "World's Number One Master." For this purpose, he studied hard, visited many renowned masters, and learned from all schools of thought. He was already gifted in martial arts, and his obsession with it made him a formidable opponent even in his youth, remaining undefeated until he met that older person. This older person once traveled the world but now lived in an ordinary town. Hearing talk of this person's unparalleled martial art skills, the fighting spirit was rekindled in Wu Ming's empty heart and he stepped forth to challenge this person. His challenge ended not in victory, and he tasted defeat with the sword, spear, and halberd against that person's stick. After his consecutive losses, Wu Ming became obsessed with surpassing this mighty opponent. For several years after that first challenge, Wu Ming challenged that older person annually, and was defeated every time. He could not figure out how victory still eluded him though he had surpassed his opponent in strength, agility, and skill. During his last challenge, a group of bandits called Reapers invaded the town where the older person lived. Wu Ming tried to flee-human flesh is no shield against heavy mech after all-but the older person, with his strength, struck the invaders with his stick and subdued three Reapers, ensuring the town's safety. However, he had also exhausted his strength in this last battle and death came swiftly upon him. Wu Ming, witnessing this event, realized the true meaning of being a warrior: True righteous ideals and belief are the key to transcendence. And so, he took on the mantle of his late opponent and embarked on his journey of chivalry under the alias "Wu Ming", or "The Nameless One".

pages.title: Eleanor
text: Ever since she was young, Eleanor had always wanted to make a name for herself as the mastermind detective of Oestermore—pursuer of criminal evildoers! Upholder of truth and justice in her fair city! Unfortunately, none of those compliments could be applied to her until much more recently. It is true that Eleanor pursued a part-time career as a private detective-for-hire in Oestermore for many years, where she'd hoped to make a real difference to her city. The reality was that demand for private eyes in Oestermore was low. The place was just too peaceful. Requests in those early days were mostly of the "runaway cat stuck up a tree" variety. What was an aspiring private eye to do in peaceful Oestermore? Even Eleanor's talented young robo-dog "Chieftain" virtually never had the chance to practice chasing down a stray cat, let alone robber. But just like that, out of nowhere, everything changed—for her and for Oestermore, forever. Cities like Oestermore are breeding grounds for myths and legends, myths that never much concerned Eleanor who always felt herself far too sensible for such nonsense. This changed however when an invite came to investigate one such urban legend of an "underground monster" that "lived in the sewers of Ostemore". This invite was accompanied by a hefty wad of cash. Eleanor suppressed the urge to refuse. After all, how could she satisfy a client looking for supernatural horrors? But she needed money and the money was good. "I guess proving an urban legend is false is also a kind of detective work... especially if someone thinks it's valuable enough to feed me." Investigating an urban legend of a massive sewer monster demanded expert advice. Eleanor roped in Gisela the artisan for a small consulting fee. The latter already seemed to know quite a lot about various myths and legends—everything it seemed except "Jumping Jack" sightings about which she seemed completely ignorant. Not that this mattered. Other legends could wait. The dynamic "Sewer Ops" duo began the long and difficult task of getting underneath the city and raking up whatever muck they could find. But the urban legend was also evolving. What had started as a neighborhood in uproar over strange nightly noises soon grew into reports of missing persons often near sewer entrances! Interest was developing in the case, especially from the neighborhood where residents were going missing. As the case heated up, Eleanor, Gisela and "Chieftain" began the long task of mapping the labyrinth network of ancient sewers underneath Ostermore. Eleanor wasn't sure what she expected down there in all that dark and damp. As she bid farewell to Gisela who went down another side tunnel, Eleanor turned around and suddenly found herself face to face with a rifle muzzle pointed at her eyes. At that distance the man couldn't miss... "ARGH!" The man cried out as "Chieftain" threw its jaws against the arm holding the rifle. It was the only split second Eleanor needed to unleash her long-practiced martial arts head-kick. Safely tied up, the man refused to divulge who he was or what he was doing until Gisela revealed a vibrating "Teeth Remover" invention for otherwise inoperable root canals. "You can tell us who you are or you can be my first test subject!" she cried. "OK! I'll talk, I'll talk!" came the man's desperate plea. The mystery was fairly straightforward. After Phaethon had been expelled from Oestermore all those years ago, they had continued to cherish the hope of one day reclaiming the bastion of technology. However, the city's defenses had been so enhanced in the intervening years that a direct attack was no longer possible. Instead underground was the best way to invade—attacking Oestermore from its roots, as it were. Once divulged, the rest of Phaethon's puzzle fell into place. The giant "sewer monster" was in fact a large digging machine. The disappearances were actually kidnappings of those unlucky enough to cross Phaethon's path, pressed into the service of their massive tunneling project. Once Eleanor and Gisela realized the truth they also realized there was no time to send a message back to Oestermore's military. Their one and only chance to shut down this secret invasion was now before Phaethon could take countermeasures! Thus Eleanor and Gisela cemented their reputations as heroes by venturing deeper underground into Phaethon's base. While Eleanor distracted the guards with a combination of surprises, bullets, and martial arts, Gisela took control of the giant digger. As the machine roared to live within the confines of Pheathon's tunnel base, confused shouts quickly turned to terror as the digger began bulldozing Phaethon's own facilities. The soldiers fled into the darkness of the tunnels from whence they came and the kidnapped villagers were rescued. Eleanor and Gisela's actions that day went down in Oestermore history. Both were honored with a splendid awards ceremony in front of the city. Naturally this breathed significant life into Eleanor's failing detective business. Fresh off their famous victory, the two have branched out into other myths, legends, and potential evil activities in Ostermore. "Gisela has been wonderful to work with. We just can't accept any commissions in relation to Jumping Jack for some reason. So... don't ask."

pages.title: Aiden
text: Aiden the "Firecracker" has always taken on life's challenges with boundless enthusiasm, whether in the dangerous world of the Arena or more dangerous world of Fire Crystal mining. The secret to his success? Not the Fire Crystal-powered mechanical arm—although that helps—but a willingness to brave any obstacle. Gone are the days when Aiden needed to mine Fire Crystals to survive. Aiden has already made the transition to potential arena champion as part of a new generation of contenders eager to unseat Hector "The King". Hector has even come close to losing his crown against Aiden in several matches of pure skill and fighting spirit—their battles are always sold out as the hottest attraction on the Tundra. For it is in the clash of steel, the lighting of flames with Aiden's iron fist that the cheering onlookers truly find refuge from the bitter cold. "I'm sending a message to Hector with this iron fist: this arena has a new champion!" "This pipsqueak calls himself the 'Firecracker'?! The only firecrackers I know are the ones I blow up, haha!" Hector and Aiden have made a game of playing up their rivalry in front of fans with their pre-match insults. But if you think this would make them enemies—as most assume—you would be wrong. The two might even be called fairly good friends outside the arena spotlight. After all, it was Hector who extended a helping hand Aiden's way after his tragic accident and provided his first big break. Hector and Aiden may be friends in private, but that doesn't mean they hold back from defeating each other in the arena. Even Hector has admitted, "The kid's got the skills to put me into early retirement one day. It's just a matter of time." Aiden grew up enjoying arena matches and was known among friends as a diehard fan of Hector. As an adult, Aiden got a job as a miner working the dangerous Fire Crystal shift—which gave him plenty of downtime to practice his own arena fighting skills. Aiden began participating in arena youth games in the hope he might be able to play competitively one day. But all those dreams seemed to fall apart when tragedy struck. Fire Crystal mines are safeguarded by delicate machinery used to keep the dangerous energies emanating from within to a minimum. For some reason a key safety controller suddenly failed during Aiden's shift and the crew chief gave the order to evacuate. This particular mine was located right next to a small city. Aiden knew that the worst-case scenario would see many townsfolk die when the mine exploded. Ignoring the order to evacuate, Aiden dove back into the heart of the mine and with quick thinking fixed the safety controller well enough to initiate an orderly shutdown. Unfortunately this also exposed Aiden to dangerous levels of unstable Fire Crystal energy at the moment he had zero protection. He blacked out, fully expecting these to be his last moments on earth... "They found him with an arm that was already crystallized beyond repair," Dr. Philly recounts the massive effort that went into saving Aiden's life, "The exposure should have killed or driven him insane. Maybe it was the tolerance he'd built up or an incredibly strong will to survive that let him leave there alive." Aiden's heroic actions became the talk of the city, and Hector himself paid a personal visit to his "number one fan". Hector also helped to organize an effort to take care of Aiden's short-term needs and said that once Aiden was back on his feet the offer was always open to come verse him in the arena any time. Even Logan from the Dawn Alliance got involved, customizing a mechanical arm for Aiden's deformed limb. The bionic arm accomplished two purposes: preventing the crystallization process from spreading to the rest of Aiden's body while also allowing him the use of his arm again but powered by a virtually limitless supply of his own crystalline energy. The bionic arm proved the tipping point in Aiden's recovery. Aiden found himself back on his feet and accepting Hector's invitation of a friendly match less than six months after his tragic accident. When Aiden strode into the arena then it was as a man reborn, full of hope, and with a fancy new nickname: "The Firecracker".

pages.title: Hank
text: Atop the vast tundra lie regions where humanity struggles to survive, whether due to harsh terrain or wild beasts. The mission of the Icebreaker Alliance is to conquer these perilous lands and expand the horizons of human civilization to survive this long winter of raging winds and heavy snow. Hank belongs to the Icebreaker Alliance as one of its fearless pioneers. Gifted with tremendous strength and great courage, Hank has developed immense willpower through his decades of pioneering adventures, including countless clashes with bandits amidst the lawless icefields. Through all those battles, Hank mastered the art of wielding a variety of hand tools as weapons, allowing him to take on up to ten enemies at a time. The Icebreaker Alliance's most celebrated achievement has to be the establishment of Arena tournaments that swept across the tundra, of which Hank is a massive fan. He knows the stats of every Arena legend by heart, possesses a deep understanding of Arena tactics and formations, and he's even put forth new strategic concepts of his own. Armed with such strength and skill, Hank could certainly find success in the Arena himself, but he seems happy to remain a spectator. Anyway, the tactics he learns from watching matches are all useful in his everyday combat work. Hank might seem like just another tough guy, but he's also got a tender heart. His chainsaw is rugged, but he can also use it to craft exquisite works of art, including carvings in ice and wood. He even dreams up fantastic stories for the lifelike figures he creates, which tundra children find enthralling. Not only that, but Hank is also a chef who specializes in desserts. Patrick often uses him as a taste-tester to sample his wildly imaginative new dishes.

pages.title: Norah
text: Norah's three defining qualities must be her remarkable courage, leadership of a light mechanized brigade, and identity as one of very few truly exceptional leaders in the Dawn Alliance.Norah and her brigade often penetrate deep into enemy territory with the speed of an arrow,undertaking reconnaissance missions, strikes, and rescue operations. And the combination of Norah's tactical brilliance, timing on the battlefield, and weapons expertise makes her an absolute nightmare for Phaethon.Norah's exceptional calmness under pressure and decisive demeanor impress even the most seasoned soldiers-even against near-insurmountable odds. If anything could possibly disturb Norah's resolve, it must be fears for her younger sister Gwen's safety. Norah may have been part of the same training cohort as Bahiti at the Academy, but the two could not be more different. Unlike Bahiti, Norah is a a master battlefield commander and tactician with little interest in anything unrelated to the intricacies of fighting since her scientist father's tragic fate.Norah has developed the firm belief no amount of knowledge can compare to what truly matters:safeguarding those she holds dear. Norah was only a child when she spotted Phaethon's columns advancing toward her father's laboratory.All her father's brilliance, his vast wealth of knowledge, proved powerless in saving him from the dreadful fate that followed. Norah stood resolute by her father's side, receiving his final testament and instructions on how to flee, all while her baby sister Gwen remained cradled in swaddling clothes. With aheavy heart, Norah carried Gwen to their father's steam-powered sled and escaped with the great driving skills he had carefully fostered.Eventually, she stopped to look back at the lab. All she could see was rising smoke. Norah and her sister were rescued by her father's colleagues at the Dawn Alliance. This encounter ignited a burning hatred for Phaethon, an unyielding dedication to her younger sister, and zeal for the path of the warrior-soldier within Norah.In the course of time Norah's younger sister has become something of a weak spot in Norah's rigid life-or perhaps Norah's only soft spot. Unlike Norah, Gwen showed extraordinary talent as an inventor, a challenge for Norah who would have preferred Gwen to focus more on ordinary combat skills. Yet Norah could not bring herself to spar against Gwen even in a controlled setting, the thought of an accident and fresh grief too much to bear. Yet Norah has since grown to value Gwen's ingenuity on the battlefield, especially when rescuing fellow soldiers.And over time Norah has gradually come to terms with the reality that Gwen has found her own strong and independent footing.

pages.title: Flint
text: Flint is the flame that is always ready to burn down Phaethon in his vengeance. It’s almost certain that his personal crusade against Phaethon will only end in either his or Phaethon's demise. Flint and his ragtag followers (most of whom have suffered at the hands of Phaethon) often partnered with the Dawn Alliance in their fight against Phaethon's forces. Bahiti and the others knew that Flint would never take an innocent life. As for criminals and wrongdoers? They won’t receive any mercy from Flint's hands. Flint was a high-ranking military officer. In a scouting mission, he got separated from his own platoon and ended up in a remote City known as “Arcadia”. That City was the closest thing to utopia - a place filled with theaters, auditoriums, and even libraries! The City did not have weapons; its citizens were peace-loving scholars, so they do not see a need for firearms. Flint fell in love with the City and the machinist Jessie. His time in Arcadia made him believe a bright future can be built even in this icy world. His hope and belief were soon destroyed in a horrible raid on Arcadia. An emissary from Phaethon showed up at Arcadia’s door and demanded the immediate transfer of all knowledge pertaining to "fire crystal". The Chief refused, knowing full well their research can be turned into destructive weapons of war. When Phaethon razed the City to the ground, Flint was the only fighter that put up a resistance. He was terribly injured during the fight but somehow survived the ordeal.His hopes for a better future are now replaced by a burning desire for vengeance. Flint and Jessie crossed paths again many years later.Embers of the couple's old affection still remained, but Jessie could not approve of Flint's all-consuming quest for vengeance. Flint will always hold a special place in Jessie's heart, but she can never bring herself to love a man dedicated to destruction. The former lovers have now drifted apart.

pages.title: Zinman
text: In the bygone era of the Sunfire Castle, Zinman was renowned as "the Greatest Architect". His understanding of architectural science and art is unparalleled. His designs were brilliant, and his reputation was oustanding. However, his appearance... let’s just say Zinman had no time for such trivial things. If not for the Great Chill, he would no doubt reach ever greater heights in his field of study. While many of Zinman's former colleagues settled in the nearest Cities, Zinman mysteriously vanished for several years. When he showed himself again, he became a key member of the powerful Dawn Alliance. Under the alliance, Zinman developed new defensive engineering techniques and improvements to the City Furnace. He takes pride in these less artistic but highly practical structures. Zinman rarely speaks of his family, but people knew of the sudden passing of his daughter. It had always been her dream to see a magnificent greenhouse full of all kinds of flowers. This project was eventually approved by the President of Sunfire Castle after Zinman spent years petitioning for it. Nearly a decade of work on the unfinished greenhouse was destroyed in the chaos following the Great Chill. Initially, Zinman could not let go of his daughter's dream greenhouse. Then reality beckoned, and he realized survival is everyone’s top priority in the frozen world. Zinman's post-Chill inventions include shelters with enhanced snow cover and conversion kits to turn nail guns into effective weapons. Although he is helping a lot of survivors with his knowledge, Zinman is painfully aware of his failure to fulfill the promise to his daughter. After joining Dawn Alliance as the chief architect, Zinman found hope and purpose again. He was glad to use his architectural knowledge to save countless lives, families, and cities. The smile on their faces offered immeasurable comfort to Zinman. He still dreams that one day far in the future, he would build that greenhouse, as an act of remembrance for his family...

pages.title: Molly
text: Most survivors loathe the permanent winter, but Molly's attitude is quite unique. She seems to greatly enjoy the wintry landscape and its new flora and fauna. After all, she can do snowball fights, bobsled runs, and build a snowman whenever she wants. But most importantly, the snowy world is all Molly has ever known. In fact, not much is known about her life before Dawn Alliance.\nBahiti found Molly during a peacekeeping operation against a Phaethon stronghold. The incredible part of the story is, Bahiti claims Molly's combat instincts were key to the team's successful escape from the heavily guarded fortress. According to Bahiti, Molly was an essential part of Phaethon’s combat program. This also explains her peculiar weapon - a snowball launcher. Although Molly seems much more interested in using it for snowball fights. Bahiti's successful rescue owed much to his ability to win Molly's trust. When a Phaethon soldier's arrow injured Bahiti, Molly flew into a rage, took down all the guards with ease, and then fled with the members of Dawn Alliance. Molly has a strange affinity for the cold. She has no problem enduring freezing conditions. Moreover, her excellent combat intuition and unusually strong fighting techniques (particularly on snow and ice) have truly piqued the Dawn Alliance's interest. What’s the source of Molly's preternatural abilities? The investigation is still ongoing. It was later revealed that Phaethon first discovered Molly in a large underground facility, where she was hibernating in a strange ‘pod’. Some believe Molly is connected to the planet in a mysterious and unexplained way. When she awakened, Molly had no memory of her past, but she exhibited superhuman vitality and physical strength. Phaethon wanted to use this and train her into an elite assassin for the organization. Fortunately, the Dawn Alliance saved her from that fate. Bahiti and the others only wish for Molly to find happiness in this strange new world.

pages.title: Philly
text: The sight of a strange masked woman can be unsettling. What does she look like behind that beaked mask? Or is it actually part of her? For that, people always stayed away from Dr. Philly, until a plague struck several years ago. The deadly disease hit the Cities without warning. The Chiefs designated a village as the quarantine spot for all those infected. Although, without proper resources, people in the village were practically left to die. When all hope was lost for the sick and forsaken, Dr. Philly chose to enter the village in search of a cure. And she succeeded. She was dubbed a miracle worker, an angel of the Cities. Philly spends a lot of time in the City graveyards and often faced accusations of grave robbery. Her studies of dead bodies are now encouraged by authorities, as her discoveries often lead to new cures for diseases. Philly is still regarded as a somewhat mysterious figure for spending long hours at the morgue and apothecary. This air of mystery made some people believe that Philly possesses supernatural power against diseases. The truth was far more mundane. Philly was a promising medical researcher in the academy before a plague claimed the lives of all her families. Philly was the only survivor in her house. After that, she became determined to push boundaries and find new treatments for the plague. Philly threw herself back into her studies with a vengeance. She has marked out disease and death as her personal enemies. And with anger came courage to face whatever dangers head on. However, Philly's goal is not just to conquer disease. She believes that one day she will be able to find a way to reverse death, even to the extent of bringing her family back...
Philly's advanced medical training immediately restores Health equal to her Attack * 200%/220%/240%/260%/280% to all friendly heroes.
A master of first aid on the point of death, Philly immediately restores Health equal to her Attack * 100%/110%/120%/130%/140% to the weakest friendly hero.
Philly poisons the target, disabling the enemy for 1s while dealing Attack* 140%/154%/168%/182%/196% damage.
Philly's secret remedy strengthens the soldiers, increasing Attack by 3%/6%/9%/12%/15% and Defense by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10% for all troops.
Philly's uses her secret tonic to enhance the warriors' strength, granting all troops' attack a 25% chance of dealing + 120%/140%/160%/180%/200% damage.
Phillys special shot improves troops focus, granting a 40% chance of reducing all troops Damage Taken by 10%/20%/30%/40%/50% .
Philly has done much to raise the strength of her herbal skills, increasing their healing effects by 70%.
Philly imparts her basic first-aid and care techniques, increasing Defender Troops' Health by 15%.

pages.title: Aisling
text: A Forest Guardian of Tair, Aisling comes from a traditional tribe steeped in respect for nature and the art of combat. One of the Forest Guardian's strongest ranged defenders, Aisling's skill with the sling is legendary. A weapon useless in most hands can exact deadly blows against distant poachers in hers. Like all good Forest Guardians, Aisling knows every nook and cranny of these woodlands, including all the best ambush spots. Most foreigners who come into contact with Aisling know her more for her extraordinary singing and instrumental skills, her songs during common festivals, or forest-fairy dances. Even the animals seem enchanted by Aisling's voice. Many animals will gather around Aisling's performances, entranced as much as any human listener. Aisling's bond with the animal world goes far beyond any typical Forest Guardian, forged in a near-tragedy. Tair legend tells of mischievous forest spirits who lead children away on lost trails from which they will never return. It is said that these children are selected for the spirit realm, but Aisling's parents refused to be comforted by this when it happened to them. For seven days and seven nights Aisling's parents encamped from forest nook to woodland corner seeking their lost baby. They finally found little Aisling inside a warm cavern surrounded by a cluster of woodland critters, sleeping soundly through the night. Since that day Aisling has displayed an extraordinary ability to understand forest-kin. Aisling sings these stories and more to her audience at many cross-tribal gatherings. But Aisling's listeners must decide the truth of it for themselves. Some say it is not beyond reason because, after all, another famous girl on the Tundra keeps a polar bear as a companion. Aisling's reputation for song and string rivals even Lynn the "bard of a thousand songs". Lynn and Aisling rejected many invitations to perform together in musical contest until chance brought them together by accident in a sleepy woodland tavern. Witnesses still tell stories of that grand meeting of musical minds. Lynn's skill in the string was shown in force that night, her music a passionate fire upon the stage. Aisling's gentle melody spoke of calm soulfulness. Two competing styles so utterly different that popular opinion could not come to a verdict. But one meaningful consequence of this music (apart from the joy of listeners) was a powerful friendship forged between Aisling and Lynn. As a Forest Guardian Aisling's sacred mission is to protect that which matters most: the holy grove. Even if withered today, scholars believe the trees that lie within Tair's sacred grove are the same species as the Tree of Life on Daybreak Island. One day perhaps the same vitality and warmth could give life to Tair's surroundings. The hope of an oasis of warmth in Tair has drawn many Dawn Alliance researchers. It has also enticed invaders and bandits full of greed in equal measure. Forest Guardians have had to pick up sling and spear as never before, and seek out new friends wherever they may be found. Though victorious for the time being, Aisling is well aware that the invaders will not stop. So the Forest Guardians have reluctantly partnered with the Dawn Alliance, which also seeks to unravel the true mysteries of the sacred grove.
Aisling flings out a fast-growing enchanted seed that quickly envelops nearby enemies for Attack* 200%/220%/240%/260%/280% damage and a 2-second stun.
Aisling uses the sacred fruit of the deep forest to restore Health of the ally hero with the lowest remaining Health equal to Attack* 120%/140%/160%/180%/200% .
Aisling's scalpel stones rival the sharpest blades, granting normal attacks a 25% chance of dealing Attack* 100%/110%/120%/130%/140% additional damage to targets.
Aisling's knowledge of the tribal harmonies of nature enthrall her troops, increasing their damage dealt by 4%/8%/12%/16%/20% .

An expert in the use of long-range forest warfare, Aisling's Marksmen deal 30%/60%/90%/120%/150% extra damage every 3 turns while exhausted enemies are forced to reduce their damage by 6%/12%/18%/24%/30% for 1 turn.
Aisling embodies the fury of the forest at a distance, granting Marksman attacks 8%/16%/24%/32%/40% extra damage against all enemy troops every 3 turns.
Aisling's forest faith imbues Wild Growth vines with a paralyzing effect, reducing target Attack Speed by 30% for 3 seconds. Fruits of Plenty also reduces target Attack Speed by 30% for 3 seconds.
Aisling's experience in defending woodland groves are of much use to Cities also, increasing Defender Troops' Defense by 15%.

pages.title: Ursar
text: Ursar's ancestors made a choice to forge a new life in the underground places of the world. Wisely or not, they believed in a source of light and healing untouched by wars above ground. There they carved out their own unique Windbreaker civilization. As one of the foremost warriors of the modern-day Windbreakers, Ursar has been brought up in the ways of battle. His courage, agility, and accuracy are unquestioned. Ursar also displays great promise as a future chieftain of the tribe, a natural leader with an encouraging word for any situation and tactical skill. Great power, responsibility, and the blessings of the ancestors will reside with him soon. Being a future chief of the Windbreaker tribe is as much a cultural career as a political and military one. This is why it is good that Ursar is very skilled in traditional Windbreaker flutes and the hand-drums, well-versed in Windbreaker dances, classical and ritual. He must also take on the role of a master storyteller to pass on the legends of his people, all the way back to the birth of the Windbreaker tribe and the creation of the world in their mythology. Tales, which as far as outsiders are able to say, contain an interesting mix of real history and myth interwoven together in beautiful poems. Many times Ursar has been asked to recount these rhymes for the benefit of Dawn Alliance explorers. And Dawn Alliance researchers have found much to like in the Windbreaker concept of the world itself being "a living being". Ursar first encountered explorers from above in their hour of need. Dawn Alliance adventurers had foolishly wandered into a toxic underground cave system covered in hallucinogenic fungal spores. Only Ursar's antidotes saved the explorers from being utterly lost. Bahiti and Ursar struck up a fast friendship that day. Windbreaker explorer Xura had already left for the surface world long before, giving Bahiti some acquaintance with Ursar's ancient dialect. Ursar was very pleased to hear of Xura glad tidings, and the two exchanged much knowledge of the under- and over-world. Ursar also shared a warning with the Dawn Alliance to stay clear of the more recent undergrounders: Thaleira and its ruler, Vulcanus. About the only good thing Ursar could say about Thaleira is they shared a reverence for the holy artifacts scattered throughout the caves. The war between Ursar's people and Vulcanus would probably be going on still were it not for the invasion of an even worse group of surface-dwellers: Phaethon. Tramplers of all that is holy, Phaethon has invaded like a swarm of locusts followed by countless bandits. The arrival of Phaethon has forced an uneasy truce between Windbreakers and the newcomers of Thaleira. Traditional warriors met the innovations of Thaleiran craftsmanship to great effect as the two sides reluctantly allied. The establishment of a Dawn Alliance outpost has also thrown new weight against Phaethon. Their greatest victory so far is winning a certain degree of freedom from fear of Phaethon.

Ursar summons a totemic Windbreaker spirit from the elders to encourage troops by increasing Attack Speed by 20%/30%/40%/50%/60% , Dodge by 10%/15%/20%/25%/30% , and Movement Speed by 25% for 5 seconds.
Ursar throws a mighty spear with power enough to inflict Attack* 100%/110%/120%/130%/140% and stun the target for 2 seconds.
The ancient Windbreaker dancers have trained Ursar well in the agility of combat, increasing Attack Speed by 10%/15%/20%/25%/30% .
Ursar is not above using the hallucinogenic spores of the underground to bewilder opponents, reducing enemy troops' Attack by 5%/10%/15%/20%/25% .

The horn of the elders encourages friends and terrifies foes, increasing Lancer and Marksman Lethality by 6%/12%/18%/24%/30% for 2 turns and reducing enemy troops' Defense by 6%/12%/18%/24%/30% for 1 turn.
Ursar's poison-tipped spears ensure Lancers deal 20%/40%/60%/80%/100% extra damage every 2 attacks and increase damage received by targets by 5%/10%/15%/20%/25% for 1 turn.
Adding poison to the edge of Ursar's blade ensures targets of normal attacks and Wind Tip are poisoned for Attack*30% damage every 0.5 seconds for 3 seconds. Max 3 stacks.
The drumbeat of the ancients is a call to arms for every warrior spirit, increasing Rally Troops' Attack by 15%.

pages.title: Natalia
text: "Natalia knows the scientific and common names of every species of flora or fauna".Above is Bahiti’s impression of Natalia, the young prodigy. Natalia possesses knowledge far beyond her years, having studied ecology, geology, and astronomy. Yet Natalia's most extraordinary ability is to communicate with and befriend wild animals. She is a good companion for fellow survivors as well, although she tends to talk non-stop on topics of of her own interest. Natalia was little more than a baby when she met the grizzly cub Kasia. The cub was separated from its family, and wouldn’t have survived in the wilderness alone. Natalia and her father took Kasia in and raised it into a strong beast. The two were inseparable, and the cross-species bond is strong. After the passing of Natalia’s father, they depended on each other and survived together in the long winter... Natalia's father Tyle is a "planetary ecologist". By comparing soil samples throughout the years, Tyle concluded that the global cooling process might be slowing, and could even reverse at some point in the near future. This observation filled him with optimism. Tyle had also begun work on self-sustaining heat sources with experimental fire crystals. Even Phaethon took great interest in Tyle's work and began to sponsor his research... Tyle's fire crystal technology was the greatest accomplishment of his scientific career. It had the potential to help all humankind, but can also cause disasters in the wrong hands. Tyle soon realized his sponsor was much more interested in personal gains than the greater good. Tyle passed his most crucial research notes to Natalia before his death at Phaethon's hands. He hoped that Natalia might finish his designs. Tyle’s noble sacrifice continues to inspire Natalia.
Natalia's bear violently smashes the ground, knocking back enemies in range and stunning them for 1s, while dealing Attack* 160%/176%/192%/208%/224% Area of Effect Damage.
Natalia wields her whip against a target for Attack* 150%/165%/180%/195%/210% damage.
Only fools would dare anger Natalia or her furry companion. Natalia has a 10% chance of gaining a + 4%/6%/8%/10%/12% Attack boost for 3s upon taking damage (max 5 stacks).
Natalia Commands the beasts to cover your troops, granting a 40% chance of reducing all troops' Damage Taken by 10%/20%/30%/40%/50%
Natalia is a natural leader, increasing Attack by 5%/10%/15%/20%/25% for all troops.
Natalia's unexplained connection with nature allows her to rally wild beast, increasing damage dealt by 5%/10%/15%/20%/25% for all troops.
Natalia exhibits the ferocity of a polar bear on the field, inspiring friendlies even in her absence, increasing all troops' Attack and Defense by 2%/4%/6%/8%/10%
Natalia and the Polar Bear are in perfect synchrony, increasing damage dealt by 30%. (maxed)
Natalia summons a herd of beasts to join the rally, raising the rallying Troops' Lethality by 15%. (maxed)

pages.title: Sonya
text: Sonya is the chief engineer on The Neptune, a submarine. Despite only joining the crew a few years ago, she has risen as a queen-like presence on the submarine. The rundown vessel is spared from frequent breakdowns, thanks to her exceptional skills. Just like the captain, Sonya longs to find the "Sunken Nation", but she is only interested in the treasure. Some are surprised by her belief in the elusive legend, given how rational and wise she is. The truth is, Sonya had already secured clues leading to the underwater nation from various ancient ruins around the world even before joining The Neptune. She believes she will find her long-desired treasure with her wisdom and Hendrik's vessel. Initially, Sonya boarded The Neptune as a prisoner. When Captain Hendrik realized she could let herself free using her skills and intelligence, and no one could stop her, he simply allowed her to roam freely on the vessel. Everyone knows that Sonya and Hendrik are merely using each other. Once there is a conflict of interests, they will turn against each other. At least for now, their "partnership" has been going well. The crew members find Sonya intimidating not only because of her physical prowess but also because she knows everyone's secrets and weaknesses and how to exploit them. Sonya's desire for wealth stems from her past. As a distant relative of the old kingdom's royal family, she used to live an extravagant life but lost everything on the day Sunfire Castle fell. Years of homelessness and destitution gave her a hard time and stripped her of dignity. Although she has gradually mastered the law of survival in the icy post-apocalyptic world, she finds herself increasingly convinced that money is the sole path to redemption and the ultimate truth! Hence, she spares no effort in seeking the opportunities to get rich. Her outstanding knowledge and combat skills gained during her time as a wanderer drew invitations from the Dawn Alliance, the mercenaries, and even the Phaethon. However, she was not satisfied with the "meager" pay they offered, so she focused all her attention on the treasures across the world instead. During her treasure hunt, she stumbled upon clues regarding a "Sunken Nation." She intentionally got herself captured by Captain Hendrik, as she needed his expensive vessel to locate the mysterious realm hidden underwater. She believes that once she discovers the lost treasure, she will become the wealthiest person in the entire tundra. She will then rebuild the kingdom of Solaris and crown herself as the new queen.
Sonya shoots jets of cryogen, freezing a target for 1.5s and dealing Attack* 220%/240%/260%/280%/300% Area of Effect Damage to the target and nearby enemies.
Sonya fires a frozen bomb, dealing Attack* 100%/110%/120%/130%/140% damage to an enemy and reducing the Attack Speed of nearby enemies by 50% for 3s.
Sonya’s burning desire for bounty propels her into a frenzied state on the battlefield, increasing her Attack by 10%/15%/20%/25%/30% .
“Everyone has a share when the legendary ocean treasure is found!” Sonya’s promise inspires everyone, increasing Damage by 4%/8%/12%/16%/20% for all troops.
Sonya motivates her Troops with bounty, making her Lancers deal 15%/30%/45%/60%/75% more damage every 2 attacks and increasing Attack by 5%/10%/15%/20%/25% for all troops for 1 turn.
Sonya’s Lancers will seize every chance to launch a surprise raid like underwater currents. Her Lancers deal 50%/100%/150%/200%/250% damage every 5 turns and stun the target for 1 turn.

Sonya sets up turrets that spurt out streams of water, increasing Defender Troops Lethality by 15%.

pages.title: Renee
text: The wandering caravan attracts attention wherever it goes. Mia's fortune-telling mesmerizes the adults,and Renee the clown is a favorite with children with her juggling and magic tricks. Renee also prefers spending time with children. Although Renee has a mind with thoughts that jump around too much for people to follow, she has an incredibly relatable personality and can easily makepeople open up their hearts to her. In addition, her performances also seem to have magic that can healthe soul, and make gloomy and hurt souls find joy again. However, like the other members of the caravan,Renee has secrets of her own too. No one knows what's hidden behind that mask covered with paints Once, Mia's caravan was attacked by a group of bandits but they cried and ran screaming after seeing Renee's face. Because of this, all sorts of rumors spread about Renee's face. Some curious people sneaked into the tent set up by the caravan to have a look at Renee's terrifying face, but there was nobody in there. They turned back and were about to make their escape when they ran into Renee, who was returning. Unprepared, the intruders fell to the floor in fright, peeking between their fingers at Renee whose ghastly face was... not ghastly at all, but kind and friendly. They were not hurt due to their reckless actions either. It was not a ghastly face that had scared off those bandits, but a potion that made people fall inton ightmares called "Dream Mold" that Renee uses to fight and to defend herself. Renee has some immunity to these substances due to long term exposure to unstable Fire Crystals as a victim of an evil experiment, where her mind had been damaged. As Philly said, "No one can make someone who's already insane go mad after all."Renee is not sad about her state, since she sees the world as a fairytale kingdom full of rainbows and lush green nature. Her companions are animals and elves, and those with ill-intent are transformed into evil magical creatures. In Renee's view, she is in a wonderful land fighting bad monsters that want to disturb the peace. Long ago, Renee was a resident of the lost city of Arcadia. As a researcher, she worked towards finding a way to communicate with the will of the world with Fire Crystals, and to uncover the truth of why the world had changed. Renee was captured when Phaethon sacked Arcadia, and forced to forcibly connect with the world's will, though her research was not yet perfected. Her will was assaulted horribly and destroyed in the process of coming into contact with a large number of unstable Fire Crystals, and her mind shattered completely. As her last shred of sanity was shed, unimaginable strength burst from her, and she broke free from Phaethon's clutches.She was the only living person left in the huge laboratory when she was discovered by others.From that moment on, "the world she sees" included the melting of ice and snow.

Renee's colorful ball explodes and release a strage cloud, dealing Attack 100%/110%/120%/130%/140% Area of Effect damage to ennemies and confuse them for 1s. Confused ennemies attacks all surrounding targets, friend and foe.
Renee splashes dreamy paint, dealing Attack 50%/55%/60%/65%/70% damage to targets and placing a Star Mark target's damage taken by 2%/3%/4%/5%/6% for 4s.
